item.title: Physical activity and exercise in individuals dealing with cancer in the Free State: A KAP study
item.description: Background: Despite therapeutic advances, cancer remains a disease with a huge impact worldwide. Exercise and increased physical activity (PA) not only prevent cancer but also mitigate the effects of the disease and treatment-related complications. item.title: Clinical readiness of third-year physiotherapy students: Perspectives of academics in South Africa
item.description: Background: In a traditional South African undergraduate physiotherapy curriculum, students can be expected to evaluate and treat a non-complicated patient at a 3rd-year level. While students are expected to apply classroom knowledge in clinical settings, some struggle to transfer theoretical knowledge and skills into clinical practice. item.title: Perspective on the integration of physiotherapy in cancer care in KwaZulu-Natal
item.description: Background: Cancer rehabilitation is vital for managing treatment-related complications such as pain, fatigue, weakness, swelling, and respiratory difficulties. Physiotherapy addresses these challenges through manual therapy, electrotherapy, chest physiotherapy and structured exercise programmes. item.title: Ethics topics in undergraduate physiotherapy curricula at South African universities: A document analysis
item.description: Background: Physiotherapy practice, professional autonomy, technological advancements, and the complexity of health and social systems require that undergraduate physiotherapy curricula include suitable ethics topics that equip students with knowledge, skills and attitudes in ethics. item.description: Background: Social accountability represents the social contract between medicine and society, encouraging healthcare professionals (HCPs) to address social and health-related issues. item.description: Background: Forensic auditing safeguards patients’ funds by investigating billing irregularities of claims submitted to medical schemes. item.description: Background: When a traumatic spinal cord injury (TSCI) happens to healthy individuals, it requires an adjustment to life situations in the community. item.description: Background: Osteoarthritis (OA) of the knee is a common, disabling condition influenced by multiple biopsychosocial factors and often requiring a total knee replacement (TKR).
